description: One-sided merge (A == Base) whose result must equal B exactly. B deletes `int gap = 0;`, so every later line in B's frame shifts up one: B's `System.out.println(x)` lands on line 6, the same line:col as Base's `y = y + 1;`. The sub-expression span filter in reconstitution - which exists to drop `a + 2` from inside `a = a + 2` - would then read the shorter span as nested in the longer one and DROP `y = y + 1` from the merged program, printing 5,2 where B prints 5,3. The filter therefore requires the two vertices to share a contributor: a genuine sub-expression always comes from the same version as its statement.
